claim.excerpt: We observed that the average blood concentration of methadone found in adult cases is 503 ng/mL, higher than observed in children, and overlapping with the range of concentration normally reported in living patients undergoing MMT (400–1000 ng/ml).

proposed_value.context_label_correction: P5 label 'clinical intoxication' replaced: excerpt and title describe post-mortem deaths.

sources.title: Characterizing post-mortem blood concentrations in methadone-related deaths

why_it_matters: Concentration values are often misread as thresholds; the reviewer must confirm specimen, population, statistic and that the value is reported in context only.

conflicts.question: Does a post-mortem methadone blood concentration distinguish toxicity from therapeutic use?
conflicts.note: The source states that the mean adult post-mortem concentration (503 ng/mL) overlaps the range reported in living patients on maintenance treatment (400–1000 ng/mL).

limitations: The 400–1000 ng/mL range quoted alongside refers to living patients in methadone maintenance treatment, not to this cohort.
